core/ai/engine_router.py - resolve which inference engine to actually use.

**"本地优先，在线次之"** is the single source of truth for engine selection.

The UI exposes an *preference* radio (online / local) but the *actual* engine
used for a recipe inference is decided here, so the user never has to remember
to flip the radio:

    user prefers local  ->  local ONLY IF the local engine is genuinely usable
                            (model file present AND llama-cpp-python bundled);
                            otherwise fall back to online with a logged reason.
    user prefers online ->  online.

A local engine is "genuinely usable" when:
    1. a model path is configured,
    2. the file exists on disk,
    3. llama-cpp-python is importable (bundled in the installer).

Note: the V.2.0.0 installer bundles llama-cpp-python (collect_all in spec),
so ``_local_engine_available()`` returns True as long as the GGUF file exists
and the PyInstaller build included the engine DLLs.

Redirect None stdout/stderr to devnull before importing llama_cpp.

    In a PyInstaller windowed build stdio may be None; llama-cpp-python's
    import-time log callback prints to stderr and a None stderr inside a C
    callback causes access-violations on Windows.

Return (engine, reason).

    engine ∈ {"local", "online"}. reason is a human-readable string good for
    the status bar / log so the user understands *why* a particular engine ran.
